# glinet_wireguard_client_config (Resource)

Manages a WireGuard client configuration in a group of the user (`wg-client.add_config` in the router API, a peer in the API). Create and update fail when the group is not a group of the user (Manual in the web UI). The resource does not start or stop the tunnel. **Warning:** the web UI shows the configuration of the running tunnel as read only. An update or destroy of the configuration that the tunnel uses can stop or restart the tunnel; this is not tested on a router. Destroy removes the configuration from the router. Import the configuration with `<group_id>/<id>`, for example `terraform import glinet_wireguard_client_config.example 1234/5678`. The write of this resource was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glinet_wireguard_client_group" "home" {
  name = "home"
}

# The keys are made up. Keep real keys out of the configuration, for example in a sensitive variable.
resource "glinet_wireguard_client_config" "home" {
  group_id      = glinet_wireguard_client_group.home.id
  name          = "home server"
  address_v4    = "10.0.0.2/32"
  private_key   = "FAKE+PRIVATE+KEY+FOR+DOCS+ONLY+00000000000A="
  public_key    = "FAKE+SERVER+PUBLIC+KEY+FOR+DOCS+0000000000A="
  preshared_key = "FAKE+PRESHARED+KEY+FOR+DOCS+00000000000000A="
  endpoint      = "vpn.example.com:51820"
  allowed_ips   = ["10.0.0.0/24", "192.168.1.0/24"]
  dns           = ["10.0.0.1"]

  persistent_keepalive = 25
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `address_v4` (String) IPv4 address of the router in the tunnel, with or without a prefix length, for example `10.0.0.2/32` (`address_v4` in the router API).
- `endpoint` (String) Host and port of the WireGuard server, for example `vpn.example.com:51820` or `[2001:db8::1]:51820` (`end_point` in the router API).
- `group_id` (Number) ID of the group, for example `glinet_wireguard_client_group.example.id` (`group_id` in the router API). Changing it replaces the configuration.
- `name` (String) Name of the configuration (`name` in the router API): 1 to 64 characters, not only spaces, without a `.` at the start and without `~`.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) Private key of the router in the tunnel, 44 characters of base64 (`private_key` in the router API). The router returns it in each read, so it is in the Terraform state.
- `public_key` (String) Public key of the WireGuard server, 44 characters of base64 (`public_key` in the router API).

### Optional

- `address_v6` (String) IPv6 address of the router in the tunnel, with or without a prefix length, for example `fd00::2/128` (`address_v6` in the router API). The provider sends `ipv6_enable` `true` when it is set and `false` when it is not set.
- `allowed_ips` (List of String) IP networks that go through the tunnel, for example `["0.0.0.0/0", "::/0"]` (`allowed_ips` in the router API, one string with `, ` between the items).
- `dns` (List of String) IP addresses of the DNS servers in the tunnel (`dns` in the router API, one string with `, ` between the items). When it is not set, the provider does not send it and keeps the value of the router. To remove a value from the router, replace the resource.
- `listen_port` (Number) UDP port of the router in the tunnel, from 1 to 65535 (`listen_port` in the router API). When it is not set, the provider does not send it and keeps the value of the router. To remove a value from the router, replace the resource.
- `mtu` (Number) MTU of the tunnel, from 576 to 65535 (`mtu` in the router API). When it is not set, the provider does not send it and keeps the value of the router. To remove a value from the router, replace the resource.
- `persistent_keepalive` (Number) Interval of the keepalive packets in seconds, from 1 to 65535 (`persistent_keepalive` in the router API). When it is not set, the provider does not send it and keeps the value of the router. To remove a value from the router, replace the resource.
- `preshared_key` (String, Sensitive) Preshared key, 44 characters of base64 (`preshared_key` in the router API). The provider sends `presharedkey_enable` `true` when it is set and `false` when it is not set.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) ID of the configuration, which the router gives (`peer_id` in the router API).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is <group_id>/<id>.
terraform import glinet_wireguard_client_config.home 1234/5678
```
